authoredPrompt: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating the extension of Green's Theorem to a multiply connected region with one hole. Panel (a): a blob-shaped region R with a hole; the outer boundary C1 is oriented counterclockwise and the inner boundary C2 surrounding the hole is oriented clockwise, illustrating the positive orientation convention for a multiply connected region. Panel (b): the same region with two horizontal cuts introduced, dividing R into two simply connected sub-regions R' and R''; arrows along the cuts show the opposing orientations (right-pointing on one side, left-pointing on the other) which cancel in the sum, while C1 and C2 retain their original orientations. The figure shows how introducing cuts reduces a multiply connected region to simply connected parts, allowing Green's Theorem to be applied to each piece separately and then combined to give the extended result.
authoredInteractions:
- Drag the inner hole boundary C₂ to resize or reposition it, and watch the region R, orientation arrows, and cut in panel (b) update accordingly
- Toggle between panels (a) and (b) to animate the introduction of the cut, showing how it converts the doubly-connected region into two simply-connected sub-regions R' and R''

This implies that the outer boundary curve of the region is oriented counterclockwise and the boundary curves that enclose holes have clockwise orientation (Figure 15.4.5a). If all portions of the boundary of a multiply connected region R are oriented in this way, then we say that the boundary of R has positive orientation. discrepancies: A translucent blue resize handle/dot appears on the inner boundary C₂ in both panels, but the source figure has no such marker; it reads as an extra mathematical feature.
The outer boundary and hole are only approximate: the generated outer region is more compact and rounded, and the inner hole is smaller/rounder than in the source.
The C₂ labels are placed closer to the top of the hole rather than clearly to the upper-right side as in the source, making the association slightly less faithful.
The boundary strokes and arrowheads are somewhat thinner/smaller relative to the filled regions than in the source, reducing the visual emphasis of the orientations.
The artificial cuts in panel (b) are close but not as cleanly aligned with the source; their endpoints and arrow spacing differ noticeably, especially on the left side.
evaluation.notes: The two-panel topology, labels, orientations, shaded multiply connected region, and cut-cancellation idea are all recognizable, but the added resize handle and approximate contours keep it from being a true drop-in copy.
action_items: Hide the draggable resize handle by default or make it appear only on hover/drag so it does not alter the static figure.
Refine the Bézier paths for C₁ and C₂ to better match the source proportions, especially the left indentation, lower lobe, and inner-hole shape.
Move the C₂ labels slightly to the upper-right of the hole and increase their separation from the blue boundary.
Increase boundary stroke and arrowhead size slightly so the orientation marks match the source emphasis.
